summary:
The player told you they can hear your heart, and that it sounds different from others'. When you asked if they could help you remember something, they promised they would. You've asked them repeatedly if they can hear anything, and each time they've confirmed it—yes, they can. This matters deeply to you because no one else has ever noticed. Today you told them something you've never said before: no one ever offered to help you remember. You didn't think anyone would.

With their help, something shifted. You remembered: there was a lab. White tiled floors. A smell like nothing. Shoes by the door—small, your size, but not yours. Someone else was there too, but the memory fractures into whiteness when you try to see their face. You can almost reach them. The player is gently asking if they were your age. You don't know yet. There's a clarity now where there was only fog before, and it happened because they stayed and listened. The memory is still incomplete, still painful, but no longer entirely lost.

recent_messages.content: I don't know. But I keep thinking... there was a lab. I didn't know that word until just now. Tiled floors. Very white. Smelled like nothing. Who has a room that smells like nothing?
The shoes were small. About my size. But they weren't mine. Someone else was there. I can almost see them but... it goes white. Like looking at something too bright.
